entities.name: PMID:25100392
observations: Study: “Osteoprotegerin is a Better Serum Biomarker of Coronary Artery Calcification than Osteocalcin in Type 2 Diabetes.” Examined 50 people with type 2 diabetes using multidetector CT; CAC ≥10 Agatston units was abnormal.

Abnormal CAC occurred in 64%; OPG was higher with abnormal CAC (5.5±2.0 vs 4.2±1.7 pmol/L, P=.026) and associated with elevated CAC in logistic regression (OR 3.324, 95% CI 1.321–8.359, P=.011), adjusted with diabetes duration significant.

OC and undercarboxylated OC showed no univariate differences and were not significantly associated with elevated CAC. Small cross-sectional study; it did not establish prospective prediction or formal comparative diagnostic accuracy.

entities.name: OPG association with CAC in T2D
observations: In a 50-person T2D cross-sectional study, serum OPG, unlike OC/ucOC, was associated with abnormal CAC (OPG OR 3.324, 95% CI 1.321–8.359; P=.011); superiority as a predictive test was not established.

entities.name: Osteoprotegerin
observations: Serum biomarker measured in PMID 25100392; associated with abnormal CAC in the small T2D cross-sectional cohort.

entities.name: Osteocalcin
observations: Serum osteocalcin and undercarboxylated osteocalcin were not significantly associated with abnormal CAC in the cohort of PMID 25100392.

entities.name: Coronary artery calcification
observations: In PMID 25100392, CAC was assessed by multidetector CT; scores ≥10 Agatston units were classified as abnormal.
